correctness.rationale: Homogeneity and the age of the C-relation identify the complete named types with the extension trees. Each labelled insertion has 2m-1 positions including the stem at m leaves and is undone by deleting that label and suppressing the parent. This proves uniformity of the growth law without a probability on infinite vertices. A surviving cherry can only be destroyed by grafting to one of its two pendant edges, and grafting cannot restore a destroyed cherry. Equivalently, contracting j required old cherries before or after extending is a bijection with extensions of a reduced base with n-j leaves (the one-leaf case has a stem). The resulting extension-count ratio is (a)_{fall j}/(a+r)_{fall j}. These are the subset inclusion probabilities of the claimed law by falling-factorial Vandermonde and uniquely specify it, including r=0; the half-integral a satisfies a>c-1, and r falling factors are nonnegative or zero. For the pgf, a step gives f+alpha(1-z)f' with positive leading coefficient since alpha*c<1. At simple ordered roots of f, the signs alternate; the sign at negative infinity is opposite to that at the least root, placing all c roots in the c leftmost/intervening intervals. Taking limits handles multiplicities. Symmetric multiaffine polarization then gives stability, and the established strongly Rayleigh theorem gives negative association. Directly p2-p1^2 gives the stated strict covariance when c>=2 and r>=1; p_j=O(r^-j) gives the union estimate. An independent enumeration by all unordered root bipartitions for six labelled leaves, pruning the two new ones and retaining base AB|CD, gave exact counts 8,20,20,15 for the empty set, each singleton and both cherries respectively. The protocol, supplied output and script were inspected but the script was not run.

value.rationale: The marked survival vector answers how much specific local topology persists when extending a fixed inferred genealogy; it cannot be read off total cherry counts. The finite law avoids enumerating labelled extensions and makes that dependence precise through one shape-independent distribution and strong negative association. These are useful structural facts about the conditional uniform model, not claims of biological realism or a new general stability theorem.
